metadata.title: The Policy of the Hollow Star
metadata.author: AI Assistant
metadata.description: 1926, coastal New England. A private investigator arrives at a weather-beaten mansion to sniff out insurance fraud. The case doesn’t stay mundane for long: lies become rites, paperwork becomes prophecy, and the estate’s grounds reveal a geometry that should not exist.

suggestedTheme.reason: A text-forward cosmic-horror mystery benefits from a minimal interface that emphasizes reading, clues, and dread without visual-novel framing.

beats.name: Title Screen
beats.notes: ASSET: Dark, grainy mansion exterior photo with high-contrast lighting. AUDIO: Low wind + distant surf.

parameters.title: The Policy of the Hollow Star
parameters.author: AI Assistant

beats.name: Set Arrival Time
beats.notes: Initialize fictional time for 1926 mood and pacing. Timer HUD can be enabled later; story still works without it.

beats.name: Arrival at Haversham Grounds
beats.notes: ASSET: Long driveway lined with dead oaks; mansion silhouette. INTENT: Present as a routine fraud job; hint at wrongness in architecture.

parameters.speaker: Narrator
parameters.text:
October, 1926. You step out of your motorcar at Haversham Manor—an old New England estate with salt in its timbers and money in its stones. The insurer’s letter is plain: suspected fraud. A house fire claim. Missing valuables. A family that won’t answer questions.

The grounds are too quiet. Even the crows keep their distance.

beats.name: Front Steps: First Approach
beats.notes: First meaningful decision: professional/legal approach vs trespass. Counters: +clues for methodical work; +dread for intrusive/occult curiosity.

parameters.speaker: Narrator
parameters.question: At the front steps, how do you begin?

choices.text: Knock and present your credentials to the caretaker
choices.location: Knock and present your credentials to the caretaker

choices.text: Circle the grounds first, looking for signs of staged damage
choices.location: Circle the grounds first, looking for signs of staged damage

choices.text: Slip in through a side service door before anyone can compose a story
choices.location: Slip in through a side service door before anyone can compose a story

beats.name: Caretaker Interview
beats.notes: NPC establishes mundane cover story; player can press (clues) or soothe (trust variable). Keep it plausible but increasingly strained.

dialogTree.speaker: Mrs. Wicker
dialogTree.text:
A woman in black wool answers after a long delay. Her eyes flick to your briefcase as if it breathes.

“Insurance man?” she asks, though your badge says otherwise. “The family is resting. You’ll find no fraud here.”

choices.text: I’m a private investigator. I only need facts—dates, receipts, a look at the fire room.
I’m not here to harass you. Help me close this cleanly and you won’t see me again.
If you’re hiding something, I’ll find it. Now move aside.

beats.name: Grounds Survey
beats.notes: Seed cosmic geometry subtly: paths that don’t match distances; ash where there was no fire. Leads to hub.

parameters.speaker: Narrator
parameters.text:
You walk the perimeter. The hedges are cut with an almost mathematical cruelty. Near the east wall, the grass bears a dark stain—old ash—yet no scorch marks on the stone.

You take notes. Once, you glance back at the manor and feel an unpleasant certainty: the windows are not where they were a moment ago.

beats.name: Service Door Entry
beats.notes: Trespass path: gives earlier horror tone (+dread from prior choice). Introduce smell of brine, odd angles.

parameters.speaker: Narrator
parameters.text:
The service door yields with a tired sigh. Inside: cold air, brine, and the faintest trace of something sweet gone rotten.

Your footsteps feel muffled, as if the house is swallowing sound. The corridor’s angles are subtly wrong—like a draftsman tried to sketch a hallway from memory after a fever.

beats.name: Investigation Hub: Where Next?
beats.notes: Hub-and-spoke. markVisited prevents repetitive clue farming. Ensure generic text works regardless of prior route.

parameters.speaker: Narrator
parameters.question: You steady your thoughts. What do you investigate on the estate?

choices.text: Inspect the burned study (the claim’s origin)
choices.location: Inspect the burned study (the claim’s origin)

choices.text: Search the greenhouse and the rear paths
choices.location: Search the greenhouse and the rear paths

choices.text: Visit the family crypt on the hill
choices.location: Visit the family crypt on the hill

choices.text: Enough. Return to your car and file a preliminary report
choices.location: Enough. Return to your car and file a preliminary report

beats.name: Burned Study: Evidence Shelf
beats.notes: pickProp auto-adds item; each selection must go to an infoText describing it (MANDATORY). Each prop also increments clues/dread.

parameters.speaker: Narrator
parameters.question: In the charred study, what do you focus on?

props.name: Insurance Ledger
props.description: A half-burned ledger with stamped policy numbers and soot-black fingerprints.

props.name: Melted Watch
props.description: A pocket watch warped by heat, its hands fused at an impossible time.

props.name: Ashen Photograph
props.description: A photograph with a corner burned away; the faces seem smudged on purpose.

beats.name: Item: Insurance Ledger (Described)
beats.notes: Clue-heavy: suggests fraud, but also an occult pattern in numbers.

parameters.speaker: Narrator
parameters.text:
The ledger lists the fire claim and—oddly—three earlier policies taken out on the same wing across decades, each followed by a “loss.”

The policy numbers repeat digits in a way that feels deliberate. One margin note, written in pencil: “The adjusters will believe arithmetic before they believe the sky.”

beats.name: Item: Melted Watch (Described)
beats.notes: Horror-forward: time anomaly hint.

parameters.speaker: Narrator
parameters.text:
The watch is ruined—yet the crystal isn’t cracked. The hands are welded at 3:17.

You turn it over. Someone scratched a star-shaped hollow into the backplate, and the metal around it is cold, as if the fire avoided that shape. Your stomach tightens with a memory you don’t own: a bell tolling underwater.

beats.name: Item: Ashen Photograph (Described)
beats.notes: Connect family to cult; reveal symbol; set up keypad code clue elsewhere (3:17).

parameters.speaker: Narrator
parameters.text:
The photograph shows the Havershams posed stiffly on the same front steps. But in the burned corner, someone has scraped the emulsion away to erase a figure—tall, blurred, standing too close.

On the back: a penciled emblem, a five-point star drawn as a hollow outline, with the words “NOT A STAR—A WINDOW.”

beats.name: Greenhouse: Strange Harvest
beats.notes: Nature + cosmic biology. One prop is a practical tool (Lantern) to gate crypt interior.

parameters.speaker: Narrator
parameters.question: In the greenhouse, damp heat fogs the panes. What do you examine?

props.name: Lantern
props.description: A heavy oil lantern, recently used; the wick smells of salt rather than kerosene.

props.name: Black Soil Sample
props.description: Soil from a bench planter—dark as ink, threaded with pale fibers that twitch when touched.

props.name: Greenhouse Note
props.description: A torn note pinned under a jar lid, written in a careful hand.

beats.name: Item: Lantern (Described)
beats.notes: Inventory-gate tool. Mention faint symbol, tying to hollow star.

parameters.speaker: Narrator
parameters.text:
The lantern is warm in your hand, as if it remembers flame. The glass is etched with tiny marks—somebody’s obsessive tally—until the scratches resolve into a hollow star.

You test the shutter. The light it promises feels… dependable. That alone is a relief.

beats.name: Item: Black Soil Sample (Described)
beats.notes: Pure dread; implies non-Euclidean root network under grounds.

parameters.speaker: Narrator
parameters.text:
You scrape a pinch into a paper fold. The soil is wrong—too fine, too eager to cling. Pale fibers lace it like nerves.

For an instant, the greenhouse floor seems to drop away, replaced by a web of roots that don’t follow the rules of direction. The vision snaps shut, leaving you with shaking hands and an almost-laugh.

beats.name: Item: Greenhouse Note (Described)
beats.notes: Key clue: mentions time 3:17 and a 'gate under the hill'.

parameters.speaker: Narrator
parameters.text:
The note reads: “Do not burn the study again. Fire draws attention. The proper opening is at 3:17, when the angles soften. Use the lantern. The gate is under the hill, behind the false stone.”

Someone has underlined “3:17” hard enough to tear the paper.

beats.name: Crypt Approach: Iron Door
beats.notes: Gates crypt interior with inventory check for Lantern.

parameters.speaker: Narrator
parameters.text:
The family crypt squats on the hill, a stone mouth sealed with an iron door. Wind pushes at the weeds like a cautious hand.

The lock plate bears a shallow, hollow star. The keyhole is there—but the darkness behind it looks deeper than the hill has any right to hold.

beats.name: Condition: Do You Have a Lantern?
beats.notes: Inventory gate: prevents crypt interior without light/tool.

beats.name: Turn Back From the Crypt
beats.notes: Soft failure that reconverges to hub; no dead-end.

parameters.speaker: Narrator
parameters.text:
You pull on the iron ring and the door gives a breath of cold air that smells of tidepools. But you can’t see two inches past the threshold.

Going in blind would be bravado, not work. Not yet.

beats.name: Time Passes on the Grounds
beats.notes: Advance fictional time after each investigation spoke. Reinforces 3:17 relevance later.

beats.name: Retreat to the Car
beats.notes: Player attempts to leave early; condition checks if dread is already high enough to force the supernatural escalation.

parameters.speaker: Narrator
parameters.text:
You reach your car with the comfort of the familiar: leather seat, metal dash, a world that obeys tools.

But when you look back, the manor’s silhouette is wrong—too many corners, as if drawn by a hand that never learned perspective.

beats.name: Condition: Has the Horror Already Taken Hold?
beats.notes: If dread >= 2, the estate 'doesn't let you go' and pushes toward finale. Otherwise player can choose to return to work or leave (still leads to finale gateway via conditionBeat later).

beats.name: A Choice to Continue or Leave
beats.notes: Meaningful choice: pursue truth vs bail. Even if leaving, story routes to finale gateway (ending based on clues/dread).

parameters.speaker: Narrator
parameters.question: The engine turns over. You could go. Do you?

choices.text: Stay. A fraud case doesn’t make your hands shake—something else does
choices.location: Stay. A fraud case doesn’t make your hands shake—something else does

choices.text: Leave now and write it up as fraud with insufficient access
choices.location: Leave now and write it up as fraud with insufficient access

beats.name: The Car Will Not Leave
beats.notes: Forced escalation when dread is high: suggests the grounds are an organism/geometry trap.

parameters.speaker: Narrator
parameters.text:
The ignition coughs and dies. Again. Again.

The headlights flicker—and in their brief cone you see the driveway stretching wrong, too long, bending in on itself like a ribbon tied into a knot. The estate does not want you leaving with your questions intact.
parameters.buttonText: Swallow your pride and go back

beats.name: Crypt Interior: The False Stone
beats.notes: Keypad used as ritual/time-lock. Clues point to 0317. Wrong code loops back with dread penalty via infoText -> keypad.

parameters.prompt: By lantern light you find a false stone with four recessed numerals. Enter the code:

beats.name: Wrong Code: The Stone Listens
beats.notes: Penalty: increase dread through a setVariable beat, then back to keypad. Keeps offline; no counter-on-choice needed here.

parameters.speaker: Narrator
parameters.text:
The false stone vibrates under your fingertips—like something behind it shifts closer. Your lantern flame gutters blue.

For a moment you hear your own voice from far away, calmly describing the case as ‘mundane.’ The sound makes you nauseous.

beats.name: Increase Dread After Wrong Attempt
beats.notes: Counter updated via setVariable (not via choice). This counter is checked later by conditionBeat for endings (dread >= 3).

beats.name: Beyond the False Stone
beats.notes: Climax setup. Player chooses approach: destroy evidence vs document vs bargain. Choices modify counters/variables and route to finale gateway conditionBeat.

parameters.speaker: Narrator
parameters.text:
The stone unlocks with a wet click. A seam opens—too wide for the hill’s thickness—and your lantern reveals a stairwell descending into an architecture that disagrees with your eyes.

At the bottom: a chamber of chalked circles and ledger pages nailed to the wall like prayers. In the center, the hollow-star symbol is cut into the floor, not as a mark but as a missing piece. Through that absence, something watches—patient as deep water.

beats.name: Final Decision in the Chamber
beats.notes: Last major choice. All paths reconverge to endingGateway conditionBeat. Threshold reachability: cluesFound can reach at least 5; dread can reach 4+.

parameters.speaker: Narrator
parameters.question: How do you respond to the chamber’s ‘truth’?

choices.text: Photograph the pages, copy the policy numbers, and leave with proof
choices.location: Photograph the pages, copy the policy numbers, and leave with proof

choices.text: Pour lantern oil over the papers and set the chamber alight
choices.location: Pour lantern oil over the papers and set the chamber alight

choices.text: Speak to the presence: offer silence in exchange for release
choices.location: Speak to the presence: offer silence in exchange for release

beats.name: You Document Everything
beats.notes: Rational route, boosts clues. Reconverges to ending gateway.

parameters.speaker: Narrator
parameters.text:
You work with shaking efficiency: notes, numbers, names. The ledger pages form a timeline of ‘losses’ that is also a calendar of openings.

Your camera flash reflects in the hollow star like a pupil dilating. Something shifts, not angry—interested. You back away without turning your back on the absence.

beats.name: You Burn the Evidence
beats.notes: Destructive route: may fail if not enough clues; increases dread. Reconverges to ending gateway.

parameters.speaker: Narrator
parameters.text:
The oil catches fast. Smoke coils along lines that aren’t drafts but decisions.

For an instant the hollow star brightens—revealing not a room beyond, but a distance. A pressure builds behind your teeth, urging you to laugh or pray. You flee up the stairs as the chamber howls without sound.

beats.name: You Bargain With the Absence
beats.notes: Temptation route. Sets variable acceptedBargain. Reconverges to ending gateway.

parameters.speaker: Narrator
parameters.text:
You speak in the careful tone you use with hostile witnesses: calm, professional, controlled.

The chamber answers by making you aware of every heartbeat you have ever had. In that awareness is an offer: forget what you saw, sign your name to silence, and the driveway will untie itself.

The bargain tastes like copper and relief.

beats.name: Set Variable: Accepted Bargain
beats.notes: Boolean flag used at ending gateway to route to secret/complicit ending.

beats.name: Ending Gateway 1: Bargain Check
beats.notes: First ending gate. If player accepted bargain, route to complicit ending regardless of clues.

beats.name: Ending Gateway 2: Enough Clues?
beats.notes: Counter check for cluesFound. Threshold reachable: up to 1 (approach) +1 (caretaker/grounds) + up to 1 (study prop) +1 (greenhouse prop) +1 (final doc choice) = 5.

beats.name: Ending Gateway 3: Dread Overwhelms?
beats.notes: Counter check for dread. If high, route to consumed ending; else to ambiguous escape.

beats.name: You Leave the Estate
beats.notes: Early-exit path still flows into ending gateway chain, so counters matter. This beat preserves player agency while keeping a satisfying conclusion.

parameters.speaker: Narrator
parameters.text:
You drive away before dusk can settle into the hedges. The manor shrinks behind you, and with every mile your reasons sound more sensible.

Yet the policy numbers in your notebook look less like bookkeeping and more like coordinates. When you blink, you see the hollow star burned against the inside of your eyelids.

beats.name: Ending: The Investigator’s Report (Expose)
beats.notes: Good/competent ending: enough proof to expose fraud/cult activity, but cosmic horror lingers.

parameters.message:
You submit your report with copies, dates, and the pattern that ties the Haversham losses together. The insurer’s lawyers see fraud; the papers see scandal; the police see a family of fanatics and a trail of arson.

No one sees the geometry beneath the words.

Weeks later, a clerk asks why your photographs show a star-shaped hole where the floor should be. You tell him it’s a light leak. He believes you. Arithmetic before the sky.

Some nights you still wake at 3:17, certain something is counting your breaths—and that you proved it exists to people who cannot understand what proof means.

beats.name: Ending: A Clean Getaway (Ambiguous)
beats.notes: Neutral ending: player escapes with limited proof; suggests ongoing menace.

parameters.message:
You leave Haversham Manor with a handful of notes and a feeling you can’t itemize. Your final report is cautious: inconsistencies, uncooperative residents, suspicious accounting.

The insurer shelves the file. The world moves on.

But you do not.

When you pass a dark window, you sometimes see your reflection misaligned by a fraction of an inch—like a draft that never quite matches the finished house. At 3:17, you find yourself listening for a bell that might be underwater, and you cannot remember when you learned to fear a time on a clock.
parameters.creditsPageBody: Interactive narrative design & writing: AI Assistant

beats.name: Ending: The Hollow Star Looks Back
beats.notes: Bad ending: dread high; cosmic horror wins.

parameters.message:
After Haversham, your case notes unravel. Dates drift. Distances lie. You discover pages in your notebook that you don’t recall writing, filled with policy numbers arranged like prayers.

One evening you wake to find your room measured in unfamiliar angles. The air tastes of brine. Your watch—any watch—insists it is 3:17.

You understand then that the mansion wasn’t a place you visited. It was a shape you were introduced to.

And once introduced, you can’t stop seeing it.

The hollow star opens in the corner of your vision.

Something patient as deep water finally recognizes you.
parameters.creditsPageBody: Interactive narrative design & writing: AI Assistant

beats.name: Ending: The Quiet Policy (Complicit)
beats.notes: Secret/complicit ending: player bargains and survives by silence.

parameters.message:
You drive away as if the driveway has always been straight. Your engine purrs. Your hands stop shaking.

You file a report that is technically true and spiritually false. A mundane fraud case. Uncooperative witnesses. No actionable discrepancies.

Days later, an envelope arrives with no return address. Inside is a single page torn from an insurance ledger and a hollow-star watermark that catches the light like an eyelid.

At the bottom: your name, written in your own handwriting.

You live a long time after that, and you never wake at 3:17 again.

But you also never speak honestly about what you saw on the hill.

The policy pays out.
The silence holds.
Something remains satisfied.

characters.name: Private Investigator
characters.description: A professional snoop with a wartime steadiness and a growing dread he can’t invoice.

characters.name: Mrs. Wicker
characters.description: The manor’s caretaker—tight-lipped, precise, and afraid of saying the wrong thing in the wrong place.

story.reasoning: Structure uses a hub-and-spoke investigation (beat_7) to deliver moderate branching with reconvergence, preventing exponential growth while preserving meaningful choice. Procedural elements: (1) counters cluesFound and dread modified directly by choices/props; (2) inventory via pickProp items, gating crypt access with a conditionBeat (beat_19); (3) fictionalTime advances to reinforce the 3:17 motif; (4) a variable acceptedBargain for a distinct ending. All paths route through an explicit ending gateway chain (beat_33 -> beat_35 -> beat_36) so accumulated state determines endings: Complicit ending if acceptedBargain, Expose ending if cluesFound >= 4, otherwise dread decides between Escape and Consumed. No AI-powered beats are used.
